clauses.statement: Issue 1 (public source, bootstrap.js _structuredClone ~5224-5299): the Error branch (~5270-5275) recurses into value.cause without seen.set(value, e), so Error cycles overflow the stack and shared Errors lose identity. Intended: insert seen.set(value, e) right after construction so clone.cause===clone. Observation: the probe only statically inspects the source (no JS engine such as node is available in this environment); it exits nonzero if the defect is present. It is not a runtime reproduction.

Issue 2: the generic branch (~5281-5288) uses Object.create(getPrototypeOf(value)) and out[k]=... assignment, so an own __proto__ key invokes the setter and the clone inherits the source prototype. Intended: plain objects clone onto Object.prototype, with own keys (incl. __proto__) defined via defineProperty; Array handling stays. The probe statically detects the assignment only.

Existing tests in structured_clone_crypto_parity.rs must keep passing: ArrayBuffer/TypedArray bytes, DataView, CryptoKey cloning, and rejection of functions/symbols with DataCloneError. Also preserve Map/Set handling, Array cloning, existing seen-map cycle handling for other containers, and the Error name/message/stack copy. Not yet observed running; the test result is unknown until the host replays it.

Uncertain: whether class instances/custom prototypes should still keep their prototype (Chrome gives Object.prototype, but the CryptoKey path at ~7097 dispatches by toStringTag and may depend on it), how symbol-keyed props (line ~5295) and accessors should be handled, and whether the Error constructor and cause-defining behavior change. No runtime verification was possible without a JS engine.
